artifacts.summary: Confirms dependency task 364's settled path shape and scope rulings, verifies the corpus is currently clean, surveys the 11-script lint house convention (template: lint-state-writer-boundary.sh), and flags three concrete risks: a _comment-field false-positive hazard for naive text scans, an unresolved ~/-prefixed-path edge case, and a documented identity-notion divergence between the new lint and merge.lua's hook_identity().

memory_candidates.content: When authoring a lint that greps a JSON settings file for a specific key's value (e.g. a hook 'command' string), anchor the match on the KEY ("command"[[:space:]]*:) rather than on any substring the value might contain (e.g. a literal path like .claude/hooks/x.sh). A sibling field in the same file -- especially a top-level _comment/doc field that quotes the correct form in prose as a convention reminder -- will otherwise false-positive as a spurious match. Demonstrated concretely: agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/settings.json carries a _comment field documenting the correct hook-path convention, and a naive '.claude/hooks/' text grep across the whole file picks up that comment's own illustrative 'x.sh' as if it were a real registration.

An install-once root-files/settings.json entry fixed in the source store never propagates to an already-deployed repo whose own .claude/settings.json predates the fix -- install-once means the deployed file is copied only when absent and is never overwritten by resync. Observed directly: this repo's own live .claude/settings.json still carries a dead 'bash scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh' hook registration that the source store's root-files/settings.json template no longer has (removed by a separate completed task), because this repo's settings.json predates that removal and root-files entries are immune to resync. A source-store fix to a root-files-only entry is therefore permanently a one-way-forward fix for NEW deploys only; an already-deployed repo needs its own explicit repair, not merely a future resync.
